The AI race just moved underground — literally.

MIT Technology Review named hyperscale AI data centers a top 10 breakthrough technology for 2026. The reason cuts deeper than scale.

AI workloads have fundamentally split in two. Training demands tightly coupled GPU clusters burning massive power. Inference demands speed and availability distributed across locations close to users. These are not the same infrastructure problem — and building for one does not solve the other.

Microsoft, Google, CoreWeave, Lambda, and Crusoe are not simply adding servers. They are redesigning entire facilities from power delivery to cooling to network topology specifically for these divergent AI demands.

Why should business leaders care? Because your AI vendor's infrastructure choices now directly determine your product latency, your inference costs, and your ceiling for scale. The model is only as good as the infrastructure serving it.

The next competitive advantage in AI will not be a better algorithm. It will be better pipes.
